newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen at mercy of Wall Street moves.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen at mercy of Wall Street moves.

text.p: Belgian shares are seen at the mercy of Wall Street in the immediate term now the bulk of domestic company earnings are out of the way, with players holding their breath on Friday ahead of U.S. monthly jobs data.
"The Dow Jones is our best indicator at the moment. As long as it keeps going down we're in for some shaky days," one trader said.

On Thursday the Bel-20 leading shares index shed 1.32 percent or 27.72 points to close at 2,079.26, just four points above the session low reached after Wall Street opened lower again in the afternoon.
Volume was modest though, at about two billion francs worth of Belgian shares, with a proportion of market participants still away on Easter holidays.
"The market is deserted by investors so a few orders going through knocks share prices," a trader said.
Of the Bel-20 index components 19 were lower and only retailer GIB ended the day in the black, with a 30 franc gain to 1,600.
The retailer announced before the Easter holiday weekend that it had swung back into profit again in 1996. The stock rose on Tuesday to 1,590 but then lost 20 francs on Wednesday.
Elsewhere some of the larger losers, like cement company CBR which fell 3.82 percent to 3,275 francs, were stocks which had risen in recent days.

After a rally which began at around 2,300 francs in September, CBR has been oscillating between about 3,496 and 3,150 francs since mid-January - breaking out just once on March 12 to shoot up to 3,600.
